title: Moonshot regional budgets and device-class smoothing with preemptible-aware fallbacks
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Objective: Implement a regional allocator that enforces fine-grained tenant budget windows and smooths device-class selection to reduce spot eviction surprises while retaining cost benefits. The feature combines a short-term spot-price oracle, per-tenant burst caps (token+currency), and a device-class smoothing algorithm that prevents rapid oscillation across GPU families. When budget/headroom is exhausted, the router should degrade to pre-approved model variants (lower precision or smaller architecture) following tenant policy.

Why: Current region/tier routing can flip aggressively between preemptible and guaranteed instances when spot pricing jitters or capacity changes, causing tail-latency spikes or model-quality regressions for customers on tight budgets. This initiative aims to provide predictable cost caps, stable latency, and graceful quality degradation for budgeted tenants across regions and GPU types.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant daily and 10-minute burst caps enforceable by the allocator (token and currency accounting)
Device-class smoothing algorithm prevents more than one GPU family switch per 2 minutes per tenant under normal load
Integration with spot price oracle (5m cadence) and capacity signals for region-level decisions
Fallback chain defined and honored: fp16 -> int8-quantized -> trimmed-model-v1 -> trimmed-model-v2, with telemetry showing successful fallbacks in test tenants
E2E tests simulating spot-price spikes and capacity loss with no more than 3% SLO violations for P1 tenants during controlled experiments
Dashboard tiles in Console: per-tenant spend window, current device-class, fallback events, and prevented-eviction count
design_notes: Maintain a lightweight in-memory budget ledger with optional Redis persist for multi-host consistency
Price oracle: aggregate cloud spot/market signals + internal recent-eviction-rate to compute a composite score; sample every 5 minutes
Smoothing: exponential moving average (EMA) of device-class preference with hysteresis and a minimum hold time (120s) to avoid flapping
Fallback policy stored per-tenant in config service (Console UI) with ordering and min-quality thresholds
Admission control hooks added to serving runtime to reject or downgrade requests when budget exhausted, emitting structured telemetry for audits
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature flag behind tenant opt-in; unit + integration tests in staging
Phase 1: Canary with 5 low-risk customers (non-critical workloads) for 2 weeks; monitor evictions, SLOs, and cost savings
Phase 2: Open to all budgeted tenants with graduated default caps and UI controls
Phase 3: Remove feature flag once metrics are stable for 4 consecutive weeks
metrics: Per-tenant token spend vs cap (real-time gauge)
Device-class switch rate (per tenant, per hour)
Fallback invocation count and latency impact
risks: Ledger consistency: race conditions when multiple allocators attempt to charge the same tenant; mitigation: optimistic locking + reconcile job
Fallback quality: some tenants will experience perceptible degradation; mitigation: require tenant sign-off on fallback chains
Oracle noise: false positives from transient spot spikes; mitigation: composite score and hold windows
Operational complexity: new telemetry surfaces and UI controls may increase support load
